items.title: Tortuous Coronary Artery Fistula Closed Using a Microvascular Plug in Heart Failure.
items.abstract: Large coronary artery fistulas may result in ischemia and heart failure. A 74-year-old woman was found to have an ejection fraction of 20%-25% with apical and anterior akinesis. A large fistula from the left anterior descending artery to the pulmonary artery was identified as the likely etiology. Multiple attempts at closure failed in the setting of extreme tortuosity with nearly 180° bends. Eventually, a 5-mm vascular plug was advanced through a microcatheter and successfully deployed. Follow-up echocardiography demonstrated improvement of the ejection fraction to 40%-45% and complete resolution of the previous wall motion abnormalities. This case illustrates a reversible coronary steal-mediated cardiomyopathy. It highlights the clinical utility of microcatheter-compatible vascular plugs for transcatheter closure of anatomically complex coronary fistulas, even in elderly patients. Percutaneous closure of coronary artery fistulas with microcatheter-compatible devices improves cardiac function even in elderly patients.

items.title: Endothelial dysfunction and long-term survival in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome stages 0-3: An EASIX-based national cohort study.
items.abstract: ObjectiveTo assess the association of the endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX) with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in adults at cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome stages 0-3.MethodsThis retrospective analysis of a population-based cohort included 10,885 adults aged ≥30 years from NHANES 1999-2018, with mortality follow-up through 2019. EASIX was calculated as lactate dehydrogenase × creatinine/platelet count. Survey-weighted Cox models, restricted cubic splines, subgroup analyses and sensitivity analyses evaluated mortality associations.ResultsDuring a median follow-up of 97 months, 1,122 participants died, including 295 from cardiovascular causes. Each one-unit increase in EASIX was associated with all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.41, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.24-1.61) and cardiovascular mortality (HR 1.30, 95% CI 1.13-1.49). There was no evidence of non-linearity for all-cause mortality (P = 0.466), while the cardiovascular association was non-linear (P = 0.008). Associations persisted after additional lifestyle adjustment. CKM-stage interactions were not significant in the full cohort.ConclusionsHigher EASIX was associated with greater all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in CKM stages 0-3. Its potential role in clinical risk assessment warrants further validation.

items.title: Cardiology Support Utilization Patterns and Associated Barriers Across Northwestern Ontario.
items.abstract: The Thunder Bay Regional Health Sciences Centre On-Call Cardiology Support Service serves a geographically vast region across Northwestern Ontario where cardiovascular disease is a major burden. The objective is to analyze service utilization patterns including locations, indications, interventions, and barriers. In this 6-month prospective study, cardiologists collected data via survey on calls from rural and remote providers. Descriptive statistics and Fisher's exact test were used. The Canadian Institute for Health Information's Rural Health Systems Model was used for interpretation. Two hundred and six responses across 19 locations identified: common consultations-chest pain, dyspnea, and atrial fibrillation; frequent interventions-medical recommendations, education, and transfer decisions; key barriers-limited personnel knowledge and infrastructure. Significant associations were identified. This study characterized cardiology support service utilization across Northwestern Ontario, identifying key barriers and opportunities to strengthen rural health systems planning and cardiovascular care. These findings can inform targeted initiatives and support future evaluations.

items.title: A self-organized QTPat-based feature-engineering framework for subject-independent classification of English- and Turkish-associated EEG signals.
items.abstract: Our primary aim is to develop an automated feature-engineering framework for subject-independent classification of EEG recordings acquired from English-speaking and Turkish-speaking participant cohorts. Drawing inspiration from a quantum tunnel pattern called QTPat, we introduced a novel approach of dynamically generating directed graphs to extract textural features. For our experiments, we utilized an EEG dataset containing 1652 English sentence-EEG pairs and 1600 Turkish sentence-EEG pairs. These signals were recorded from 20 English-speaking and 20 Turkish subjects who were presented with standardized sentences in their respective native languages. During the experiments, the participants were instructed to carefully contemplate each sentence while wearing a mobile brain cap system that acquired 14-channel EEG signals. Our preprocessing pipeline involved subjecting the EEG signals to multiple filtered wavelet packet decompositions, using both 6 Daubechies and 6 symlet wavelet filters. Subsequently, we extracted textural and statistical features employing the QTPat model, along with 20 statistical moments. To enhance discriminative power, we applied neighborhood component analysis and the Chi2-function to select the most relevant features. The k-nearest neighbor classifier was then employed to calculate predictive vectors. To further refine the results, we introduced an iterative hard majority voting scheme, generating additional voted vectors. Finally, we utilized a greedy algorithm to select the best-channel-wise and overall model results. Using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation (LOSO CV), the proposed framework achieved 96.37% classification accuracy using four selected EEG channels. These findings demonstrate that the QTPat-based architecture can discriminate the two language-associated EEG cohorts under subject-independent evaluation. However, because language and participant population are coupled in the available dataset, the present results should not be interpreted as definitive evidence of language-specific neural decoding. Further studies using within-subject bilingual experimental designs are required to determine whether the identified EEG patterns specifically reflect language-related neural processing.

items.title: Patterns of cardiovascular disease subtypes and associated factors among young adults in Peshawar, Pakistan: a multicenter hospital-based cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are a major cause of morbidity and mortality. Evidence on CVD subtypes in young Pakistani adults is limited. This study characterized CVD subtypes and associated factors among young adults in Peshawar Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. A multicentre, cross-sectional study was conducted at four hospitals among patients aged 18-45 years. Data were extracted from three-year hospital records. Associations were assessed using chi-square/Fisher's exact tests and logistic regression. 8,650 CVD cases, 2,090 (24.2%) were young adults, predominantly male (64.6%), with a median age of 40 years (IQR: 36-44). ACS was the most common subtype (61.0%), followed by cardiomyopathy (39.0%). Overweight/obesity (77.0%), hypertension (56.5%), smoking (39.7%), dyslipidaemia (21.8%), and diabetes (14.4%) were the most prevalent factors. Compared with ACS, cardiomyopathy was independently associated with high heart rate, hypertension, dyslipidaemia, diabetes, and family history. Smoking was associated with lower odds of cardiomyopathy than ACS (aOR: 0.50, 95% CI: 0.41-0.61, p  < 0.001). Young adults accounted for 24.2% of CVD cases, with ACS and cardiomyopathy the most common subtypes, highlighting the need for targeted strategies. The cross-sectional design, findings indicate subtype differences rather than causal effects, while supporting smoking cessation and early hypertension detection in young adults. Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is often considered a health problem that mainly affects older adults. However, many young adults also develop serious heart conditions, which can lead to long-term health complications and place an additional burden on healthcare systems. This study examined the patterns of cardiovascular disease among young adults aged 18–45 years who received treatment at four major public tertiary care hospitals in Peshawar Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. We reviewed hospital records collected over a three-year period to identify the most common types of cardiovascular disease and the factors associated with them. Among 8,650 patients with cardiovascular disease, 2,090 (24.2%) were young adults. The two most common conditions were acute coronary syndrome (ACS), which includes conditions caused by reduced blood flow to the heart, and a broader cardiomyopathy. Overweight and obesity, high blood pressure, smoking, abnormal blood lipid levels, diabetes, and a family history of cardiovascular disease were common among these patients. Our findings highlight the substantial burden of cardiovascular disease among young adults in this hospital-based population. These results may help healthcare professionals and policymakers better understand the characteristics of young adults with cardiovascular disease and support future prevention and management strategies.

items.title: Multifunctional Magneto‑Thermal Probe Enhances the Efficacy of Tumor Therapy as a Tumor Nanovaccine.
items.abstract: Magnetic hyperthermia therapy (MHT) is an emerging thermotherapeutic approach that has shown promising potential in cancer treatment. However, conventional MHT strategies exhibit limited capacity to activate anti-tumor immune responses, an essential factor for preventing cancer recurrence and metastasis. Therefore, improving the immunomodulatory efficacy of MHT remains a critical challenge. This study designed and developed a novel magneto-thermal probe, PSRNP, by conjugating anti-PD-L1 and RS09 peptides onto the surface of superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles. The resulting PSRNP nanoprobes demonstrated excellent magneto-thermal conversion efficiency and favorable biocompatibility. In vivo analysis demonstrated that PSRNP-mediated MHT effectively remodels the tumor microenvironment. Meanwhile, PSRNP-mediated MHT showed superior immune activation effects, with a 5.14-fold increase in intratumoral CD86 + cells and a 3.30-fold increase in CD137 + cells compared with the Fe 3 O 4 -mediated MHT group. Furthermore, PSRNP-mediated MHT potentiated the therapeutic efficacy of tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte therapy and prevented tumor recurrence after surgical resection. The PSRNP probe represents an innovative platform for improving the immunotherapeutic performance of MHT in solid tumors. The findings of this study establish a theoretical and experimental foundation for advancing MHT as a synergistic cancer treatment strategy.

items.title: Dual Metabolic Inhibition Via Vanadium-NO Synergistic Nanoplatform Potentiates Cancer Immunotherapy.
items.abstract: Immunotherapy has emerged as a pivotal strategy in cancer treatment. However, tumor metabolic reprogramming not only promotes cancer cell survival but also fosters an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME), thereby hindering immune activation. To address these challenges, we developed a novel multifunctional hybrid nanoplatform, termed VTLM, via microfluidics-assisted self-assembly of bioactive vanadium species and an arginine-based nitric oxide (NO) donor. This nanoplatform synergistically modulates tumor metabolism to potentiate antitumor immunity. Specifically, we observed that vanadium species in VTLM reduce pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2) expression and enzymatic activity, which may contribute to the suppression of tumor glycolysis, while tumor cell-targeted NO release induces mitochondrial damage, ultimately enforcing a dual metabolic blockade. This strategy overcomes the metabolic plasticity of tumor cells, a major obstacle in single-pathway metabolic targeting. Importantly, VTLM-induced metabolic collapse not only drives lactate depletion within the TME but also promotes immunogenic cell death, thereby reversing immunosuppression and amplifying antitumor responses. Furthermore, VTLM exhibited marked therapeutic efficacy in a 4T1 subcutaneous tumor model, achieving an 80.7% tumor weight-based inhibition rate alongside robust intratumoral immune activation. Collectively, this study establishes a nanoplatform centered on multi-metabolic regulation, which may hold potential for further preclinical evaluation as a strategy to enhance cancer immunotherapy.

items.title: Therapeutic Peptide-Programmed Liquid-Crystalline Topology Switching for pH-Gated Postoperative Cancer Immunotherapy.
items.abstract: Stimuli-responsive depots for postoperative cancer therapy often treat therapeutic payloads as passive cargo, resulting in premature leakage and limited on-demand activation. Herein, we report a therapeutic peptide-programmed liquid-crystalline depot in which the Vpr-derived antitumor peptide (VDAP) functions simultaneously as an immunotherapeutic effector and a supramolecular topology regulator. At physiological pH, cationic α-helical VDAP was electrostatically anchored by oleic acid-containing lipid domains, reinforcing a compact inverse hexagonal (H II ) topology associated with reduced peptide diffusion. In the acidic postoperative tumor microenvironment, protonation of oleic acid could disrupt anionic anchoring, whereas histidine protonation within VDAP amplified intrachannel electrostatic repulsion. This cooperative peptide-lipid charge reprogramming could drive graded liquid-crystalline topology remodeling from a diffusion-restrictive H II organization to a more interconnected bicontinuous cubic Im3̄m network, consistent with increased pH-responsive peptide release. In an orthotopic incomplete-resection breast tumor model, the depot induced immunogenic tumor destruction, enhanced damage-associated molecular pattern release, promoted dendritic cell maturation and CD8 + T cell infiltration, and reshaped the immunosuppressive surgical bed. These results demonstrate that electrostatic-topology-gated VDAP-enabled supramolecular topology switching provides effective adaptive local cancer immunotherapy, effectively suppressing postoperative tumor recurrence and attenuating pulmonary metastasis.

items.title: Personalized allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in myelodysplastic syndromes: Integrating molecular risk, donor selection, and post-transplant strategies.
items.abstract: Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) remains the only treatment with curative potential for myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS). This review synthesizes MDS-specific evidence on transplant indication and timing, conditioning, donor choice, molecular predictors, and post-transplant surveillance. Prospective biologic-assignment studies support a survival benefit in fit older adults with higher-risk MDS. The Molecular International Prognostic Scoring System (IPSS-M), transplant-specific cytogenetic and mutational factors, comorbidity, and transfusion burden refine selection beyond the Revised International Prognostic Scoring System (IPSS-R). Alternative donors expand access, including haploidentical transplantation with post-transplant cyclophosphamide. Conditioning intensity should reflect both disease risk and patient fitness, with regimen-level scoring emerging for cord blood transplantation. Although non-relapse mortality has decreased over time, relapse remains the major unresolved cause of failure. MDS-specific measurable residual disease, graft-versus-host disease, cytomegalovirus assessment, and risk-adapted post-transplant interventions provide a practical framework for individualized care.

items.title: CAR-T Cell Therapy in Solid Tumors: Implications of Satri-cel for Gastric and Gastrointestinal Cancers.
Multifactorial Contributors to Diagnostic Delay in a High-Risk Patient with Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Case Report with Clinical Lessons.
items.abstract: Patients at high risk for primary liver cancer (PLC) are recommended to undergo PLC surveillance at least every six months. Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) is a commonly used biomarker; however, approximately 15-30% of PLC cases remain AFP-negative throughout their course. Therefore, surveillance in high-risk populations should be based on liver imaging. Any newly detected or progressive lesion should be further characterized by contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT), contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), or contrast-enhanced ultrasound, following guideline-based classification and follow-up recommendations. This case details a 45-year-old Chinese male with hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and a family history of PLC. As a high-risk individual for PLC, he did not undergo regular PLC surveillance for three years. During opportunistic encounters for acute myocardial infarction and abdominal pain, the attending specialists failed to appreciate the progression of liver imaging findings. In addition, the COVID-19 pandemic may have further aggravated pre-existing difficulties with follow-up and access to care, contributing to a delayed diagnosis of PLC. This case illustrates how a combination of physician-related, patient-related, and social-environmental factors contributed to surveillance failure and diagnostic delay in a high-risk patient with PLC. It reflects on why guideline-recommended interventions were not implemented at each healthcare encounter, how to correctly interpret AFP, and how to improve adherence to surveillance among high-risk populations for PLC. The insights from this case aim to inform systematic improvements in PLC monitoring for patients with chronic HBV infection.

items.title: The ncRNA-Epigenetic-Cuproptosis Axis in Liver Diseases: From Copper Homeostasis to Precision Hepatology.
items.abstract: Cuproptosis, a recently defined copper-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by excess intracellular copper, is characterized by copper binding to lipoylated tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle proteins, causing aberrant protein oligomerization, iron-sulfur cluster loss, and proteotoxic stress. Given the liver's central role in copper homeostasis, hepatocytes are particularly vulnerable to this death modality. This review examines the emerging non-coding RNA (ncRNA)-epigenetic-cuproptosis axis in liver diseases, critically evaluating the evidence across a spectrum from well-established biochemical principles to largely hypothetical connections. Epigenetic mechanisms, including DNA methylation, histone modifications, and N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modifications, can modulate cuproptosis sensitivity. The methyltransferase-like 3 (METTL3)-m6A- fragile X messenger ribonucleoprotein 1 (FMR1)-ferredoxin 1 (FDX1) axis, which confers cuproptosis resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) through translational repression of FDX1, represents the strongest mechanistic evidence in hepatic contexts. ncRNAs, including microRNAs (miRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), and circular RNAs (circRNAs), add additional regulatory layers; miR-133a-5p has been shown to facilitate cuproptosis in hepatocellular carcinoma by targeting ATP7B. We additionally highlight high-copper HCC phenotypes, the MYC-CTR1 and COMMD3 pro-tumor axes, and ferroptosis-cuproptosis combination strategies as priority translational directions. We systematically evaluate the ncRNA-epigenetic-cuproptosis axis across major liver diseases, including metabolic-associated steatotic liver disease, alcohol-associated liver disease, viral hepatitis, cholestatic liver disease, hepatic fibrosis, ischemia-reperfusion injury, Wilson disease, and HCC. Evidence tiers range from direct functional validation, such as copper ionophore-induced cuproptosis in HCC cells and cholestatic liver injury models, through promising but incomplete data, to largely bioinformatic associations lacking functional validation. Translational opportunities include biomarker development, copper ionophore-based therapeutics, and ncRNA-targeted interventions; we further distinguish mechanistic evidence from available human clinical data and outline how tumor copper phenotype, ncRNA signatures, viral etiology, immune context, and individual copper metabolism status could inform precision hepatology. We identify six priority questions and propose a research roadmap to advance this field from correlative associations toward rigorous mechanistic understanding, quantification of cuproptosis relative to established liver-cell death pathways, and eventual clinical implementation in precision hepatology.
items.journal: Journal of clinical and experimental hepatology

items.title: Multifocal intracranial aneurysms and a clinical diagnosis of ruptured retinal arterial macroaneurysm in presumed hepatitis B-associated polyarteritis nodosa: A case report.
items.abstract: Polyarteritis nodosa (PAN) is a necrotizing medium-artery vasculitis; intracranial aneurysms are rare. A woman in her early thirties with hypertension and hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) positivity presented with thunderclap headache, vomiting, and blurred vision. Available records described intracranial hemorrhage associated with a right posterior cerebral artery (PCA) aneurysm, but the index computed tomography/angiography images and full report were unavailable to classify the hemorrhage. The aneurysm was coil embolized with intentional parent-vessel sacrifice. Subsequent magnetic resonance imaging showed right occipitotemporal and thalamic infarction with hemorrhagic transformation-an expected consequence of right PCA sacrifice. A small acute left caudate infarct outside the treated territory raised a separate multifocal or embolic mechanism. Time-of-flight magnetic resonance angiography showed the partially occluded right P2p/P3 PCA aneurysm and 2 distal left internal carotid artery aneurysms. During the same admission, subhyaloid and intraretinal hemorrhage led to a clinical diagnosis of ruptured retinal arterial macroaneurysm; no fundus photograph, fluorescein angiogram, or optical coherence tomography angiography was available, and follow-up structural optical coherence tomography did not show the lesion. Elevated inflammatory markers, neuropathic symptoms, multifocal aneurysms, and HBsAg positivity led rheumatology to a working diagnosis of HBV-associated PAN. Because no biopsy or visceral angiography was performed and accepted classification criteria were not securely met, the diagnosis is described as presumed. The teaching point is attribution: the dominant stroke was iatrogenic; the contralateral infarct and multifocal aneurysms prompted systemic evaluation; ocular hemorrhage may be a clue but does not establish shared vasculitic causation.

items.title: Burden, healthcare utilization, and costs of chronic liver disease-related hospitalizations in California: a population-based study of trends and projections, 2005-2035.
items.abstract: Long-term trends in hospitalization burden, healthcare utilization, and costs of chronic liver disease (CLD) in the United States remain poorly characterized. Using statewide hospital discharge data, we quantified trends from 2005 to 2018 and projected future burden through 2035 across demographic subgroups. We used average annual percent change (AAPC) to quantify trends in hospitalized patients, hospitalizations, deaths, along with age-standardized rates (ASHPR, ASHR, and ASMR); hospitalizations per patient-year, average length of stay, 30-day readmission, in-hospital mortality; and inflation-adjusted hospital charges (2019 US dollars). Analyses were conducted overall and for hepatitis B virus(HBV), hepatitis C virus(HCV), alcohol-associated liver disease(ALD), and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). From 2005 to 2018, hospitalized CLD patients increased from 71,214 to 122,810 (AAPC, 4.37%; 95% CI, 3.87%-4.88%), and deaths from 11,455 to 24,560 (6.02%; 4.20%-7.86%). ASHPR increased from 275.12 to 377.88 per 100,000, and ASMR from 45.53 to 74.77. Hospitalizations and charges increased from 116,482 to 185,268 and $9.63 billion to $18.63 billion, while in-hospital mortality declined (AAPC, -7.02%; 95% CI, -8.72%-5.30%). MASLD- and ALD-related hospitalizations increased, whereas HBV- and HCV-related hospitalizations declined. Men had higher hospitalization and mortality rates, particularly for ALD. Hispanic populations had the fastest-rising burden, driven by MASLD; HBV burden was concentrated among non-Hispanic Asian populations, whereas overall CLD and ALD-related mortality were highest among non-Hispanic White populations. Findings highlight the need for targeted prevention and screening, early management of metabolic and alcohol-related risk factors, and equitable access to liver care. No funding.

items.title: Estimation of Antimicrobial-Resistant Mycoplasma genitalium Infections in People Aged 14-59 Years: Results From the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, United States, 2017-2018.
items.abstract: Mycoplasma genitalium antimicrobial resistance is common in US sexual health clinics. Population-level prevalence is unknown. We tested National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (2017-2018) specimens for M genitalium resistance mutations (n = 58). Macrolide resistance prevalence was 42.7% (95% CI, 24.4%-62.7%). Quinolone resistance was not detected. Macrolide resistance testing should guide azithromycin treatment.

items.title: Primetime for the Gasdermins Seesaw in Intestinal Homeostasis and Digestive Disorders.
items.abstract: The five pore-forming gasdermins (GSDMs, namely GSDMA-E) are best known for executing pyroptosis, a lytic and highly inflammatory form of programmed cell death. Accumulating evidence over the past decade has unveiled diverse nonlytic functions of GSDMs in digestive homeostasis and disease. GSDMs preserve intestinal barrier integrity and mucosal immunity under physiological conditions, whereas their dysregulated activation fuels tissue injury across a spectrum of digestive diseases, including inflammatory bowel disease, acute intestinal injury, radiation enteritis, acute pancreatitis, and liver disorders. Notably, the functional outcome of GSDM activation is highly context-dependent: the same protein can be either protective or injurious. This duality extends to digestive oncology, where GSDM-mediated pyroptosis can stimulate or suppress antitumor immunity. GSDM-targeted drugs, including GSDMD agonists, GSDMD inhibitors, and GSDME inhibitors, have shown encouraging efficacy in preclinical models, although none have yet reached the clinic. Here, we review the dual roles of GSDMs across the digestive system, outline the mechanistic basis of their form-, cell-, and tissue-specific functions, and discuss the progress and remaining challenges in GSDM-targeted therapy.

items.title: Hepatocyte CBX2 Safeguards Hepatic Lipid Homeostasis by Elevating Ca 2+ -CaMKK2-AMPK Signaling to Counter MASLD.
items.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects approximately one-third of adults and lacks effective pharmacological therapies. Here, we identify Chromobox 2 (CBX2), a Polycomb-associated chromatin regulator, as a previously unrecognized regulator of hepatic lipid homeostasis. CBX2 expression is markedly reduced in hepatocytes from patients with MASLD, multiple mouse models (db/db, ob/ob, HFD, and HFHC), and steatotic hepatocytes in vitro. Hepatocyte-specific CBX2 overexpression ameliorates hepatic steatosis, improves glucose metabolism, and suppresses inflammation, whereas CBX2 deficiency exacerbates these metabolic disturbances. Mechanistically, CBX2 enhances H3K4me3 enrichment at the Orai1 promoter, promoting Orai1 transcription and increasing intracellular Ca 2+ levels. Elevated Ca 2+ activates the CaMKK2-AMPK signaling pathway, leading to ACC phosphorylation, inhibition of de novo lipogenesis (FAS, ACC, and SCD-1), enhancement of fatty acid oxidation (PPARα and CPT-1a), and suppression of NF-κB/JNK-mediated inflammation. Genetic and pharmacological interventions further establish the necessity of this Ca 2+ -CaMKK2-AMPK axis for CBX2-mediated metabolic protection. Collectively, our findings reveal a CBX2-driven metabolic regulatory circuit and highlight CBX2 and its downstream signaling pathway as potential therapeutic targets for MASLD.

items.title: Cannabidiol (CBD) for Pain: A Narrative Review of Evidence to Date.
items.abstract: Cannabidiol (CBD), the principal non-intoxicating phytocannabinoid of Cannabis sativa , is widely marketed and self-administered for pain relief, yet its regulatory status as an analgesic remains unapproved. This review synthesizes preclinical mechanistic data, human pharmacokinetic data, and clinical trial evidence across major pain conditions in order to summarize the current evidence for, or against, efficacy and safety for pain. A synthesis of published information was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, PubMed Central, Cochrane Library, ScienceDirect, and other databases, integrating findings from systematic reviews, meta-analyses, randomized controlled trials (RCTs), and pharmacology reviews on CBD (independent of combination products where possible) and pain of any etiology. Preclinical and mechanistic data support plausible physical analgesic pathways for CBD, including receptor modulation, indirect enhancement of endocannabinoid tone via fatty-acid-binding-protein (FABP) inhibition, and anti-inflammatory effects. However, translation to clinical benefit has been inconsistent. In the largest meta-analysis of cannabinoids for pain, cannabinoids reduced chronic pain and improved sleep quality, but effect sizes fell below predefined minimally important clinical differences, and cannabinoids showed no benefit for acute or cancer pain, while increasing non-serious adverse events. CBD randomized trials in knee osteoarthritis, fibromyalgia, and acute low back pain have consistently failed to separate from placebo, whereas smaller/lower-quality trials and observational surveys report subjective benefit. Safety data increasingly point to dose-dependent hepatotoxicity risk. Despite strong biological plausibility and considerable consumer use, current high-quality evidence does not support CBD monotherapy as an effective analgesic across most pain conditions studied to date. Safety monitoring, particularly of liver enzymes at higher doses, is warranted.

items.title: Incidence and mortality of invasive fungal infections among patients admitted in intensive care units in India: findings from a multicentric registry-based study (2023-25).
items.abstract: Invasive fungal infections (IFIs) are challenging to treat in critical care, particularly among patients treated in Intensive care units (ICUs). The existing evidence on IFIs from India remains fragmented. This study characterises IFI incidence, risk factors, resistance pattern, treatment and outcome among patients admitted to ICUs. This multicentre observational study leveraged registry data on IFIs among patients admitted to 63 ICUs in eight Advanced Mycology Diagnostic and Research centres in India between January 2023 and November 2025. Patients with proven and probable IFI according to European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer/Mycoses Study Group Education and Research Consortium (EORTC/MSGERC) 2020 and the modified Aspergillus intensive care unit (AspICU) 2020 criteria were included. IFI incidence to hospital admission, all-cause in-hospital mortality, pathogen distribution and antifungal susceptibility were recorded. Mortality-associated factors were estimated using multivariable logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards analysis. Among 178,417 ICU admissions, 2500 IFI patients were identified with an incidence of 14/1000 admissions (95% CI 13.5-14.6) and all-cause mortality of 53.6% (95% CI 51.7-55.6%). Invasive candidiasis was the most frequently reported (57.1%), followed by invasive aspergillosis (37%), mucormycosis (3.4%), trichosporonosis (1.8%), pneumocystis pneumonia (1.1%), and cryptococcosis (1.2%). Median age of the patients was 45 years (IQR: 26-60), with 61.9% males and 38.1% females. Among candidiasis, Candida tropicalis predominated (35.6%), while Candida auris exhibited high fluconazole resistance (61.7%) and elevated amphotericin B minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) (40.7%). Aspergillus fumigatus (50.8%) and Aspergillus flavus (38.7%) predominated among culture-positive aspergillosis, with generally low MICs. Exploratory multivariable analyses showed that sepsis, chronic liver disease, immunosuppression, corticosteroid exposure, and total parenteral nutrition were associated with higher mortality in invasive candidiasis, whereas mechanical ventilation, corticosteroid exposure, and immunosuppression were associated with higher mortality in invasive aspergillosis. The study findings highlight a high IFI burden and mortality among patients admitted in ICUs of India, with mortality exceeding 50%, underscoring the need for continuous surveillance, rapid diagnostics, infection control and antifungal stewardship. This study was funded by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), Delhi (Grant ID: 157401).
